author: ValWood
body:
α subunit (Met10) – binds FAD and NADPH; it accepts electrons from NADPH and passes them along the electron-transfer chain.

β subunit (Sir1 in S. pombe, Met5 in S. cerevisiae) – binds FMN and the siroheme/[4Fe-4S] cluster. This is where sulfite actually gets reduced to sulfide,  at the metal center of the siroheme. 

https://academic.oup.com/femsyr/article/9/3/446/541267?login=false

 the two chemical half-reactions are mechanistically and biochemically separable, but coupling them into the biologically relevant NADPH-driven sulfite reduction needs the assembled complex.

@pgaudet  should this be annotated as a complex or individual subunits. I'm quite confused about these types of complexes since succinate dehydrogenase  is no longer considered divisible

author: ValWood
body: Also, I did get the wrong subunit. The beta subunit is the catalytic subunit, although sometimes the alpha subunit is called the catalytic subunit , but this is because it was cloned first

author: marcfeuermann
body:
This is so confusing, let's try to understand what we ave to do here (or not).

From the paper linked, it is not obvious since both subunits are considered as catalytic subunits...  so annotation to both as CONTRIBUTES_TO does not seem wrong.
However the rule is to split activities of each catalytic subunit and you'd like to have:
Sir1 is β subunit, so annotation to PTN001285008 should be without CONTRIBUTES_TO
Met10 is α subunit so PTN002322139 should not have the activity anymore (with  CONTRIBUTES_TO) but another catalytic activity.
Do we really want to complicate things so much that users end up just as confused as the curators ?
